title: REWIND: Uncertainty-Guided Trajectory Repair for Test-Time Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.19561v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An early mistake in the generated reasoning can constrain all subsequent reasoning. Repeated-generation methods, like MCMC-based approaches, attempt to improve output quality by sampling multiple generations, but their effectiveness can be limited by randomly selecting where to regenerate. On MATH500 with Qwen2.5-Math-7B, we find that incorrect responses have substantially higher mean token entropy than correct responses, with an average within-question relative increase of approximately 112%, suggesting that entropy can signal reasoning errors. Motivated by this finding, we introduce REWIND, a training-free controller that uses entropy dynamics to propose targeted suffix regenerations. Across three model families and five benchmarks, REWIND outperforms all baselines, with gains of 0.51-10.00 percentage points over the strongest baseline. translated_title: REWIND：面向测试时推理的不确定性引导轨迹修复
translated_abstract: 在生成的推理过程中，早期出现的错误可能会限制所有后续的推理。重复生成方法，如基于MCMC的方法，试图通过采样多个生成结果来提高输出质量，但其效果可能因随机选择重新生成的位置而受限。在MATH500数据集上使用Qwen2.5-Math-7B模型，我们发现错误响应的平均token熵显著高于正确响应，同一问题内的平均相对增幅约为112%，这表明熵可以作为推理错误的信号。受这一发现启发，我们提出了REWIND，这是一种无需训练的控制器，利用熵的动态变化来提出有针对性的后缀重新生成。在三个模型系列和五个基准测试上，REWIND优于所有基线方法，相比最强基线获得了0.51-10.00个百分点的提升。这些结果证明了有针对性的、不确定性引导的轨迹修复的有效性。
tldr: 研究发现错误推理伴随显著更高的token熵，据此提出无需训练的REWIND方法，利用熵信号定位并重新生成推理轨迹中的错误后缀，在多个模型和基准上相比最强基线提升0.51-10.00个百分点。
en_tdlr: REWIND is a training-free controller that leverages token entropy as an uncertainty signal to identify and selectively regenerate erroneous reasoning suffixes, outperforming all baselines across three model families and five benchmarks.
